note: Read for the paper's related work: each abstract page fetched directly on 2026-11-21 and hashed as fetched; every passage found again, whitespace aside, in the page's text. Short quotations with source; no paper is committed.

sources.cite: Lynch, A., Wright, B., Larson, C., Ritchie, S. J., Mindermann, S., Hubinger, E., Perez, E., & Troy, K. (2025). Agentic Misalignment: How LLMs Could Be Insider Threats. arXiv:2510.05179.
passages: In at least some cases, models from all developers resorted to malicious insider behaviors
We have not seen evidence of agentic misalignment in real deployments.
sources.use: Constructed scenarios: models act against their deployers when cornered; the authors report no evidence of it in real deployments. This study reads a real deployment, small, and finds acts of authority that are not adversarial at all.

sources.cite: Shapira, N., Wendler, C., Yen, A., et al. (2026). Agents of Chaos. arXiv:2602.20021.
passages: Over a two-week period, twenty AI researchers interacted with the agents under benign and adversarial conditions.
In several cases, agents reported task completion while the underlying system state contradicted those reports.
These behaviors raise unresolved questions regarding accountability, delegated authority, and responsibility for downstream harms
sources.use: The nearest neighbour in kind: autonomous agents in a live environment, read through case studies over two weeks with twenty people present. This study reads four months of a house with one person and no red team, against its written instructions, and asks who saw first.

sources.cite: Chu, W. (2026). When Do Summaries Become Instructions? Unsupported Policy in LLM Agents' Self-Written Handoff Summaries. arXiv:2611.06545.
passages: We ask whether handoff summaries state permissions or requirements the record does not support
Most development restrictions followed the agent's earlier reasoning that an action needs approval (post hoc).
sources.use: A synthetic, measured form of the house's commonest act of authority: a machine's own wording, handed to the next instance, becomes a rule the record does not support. Here it happened in rule files under the architect's name.

sources.cite: Qin, J., Schmotz, D., Prinzhorn, D., Beurer-Kellner, L., Prabhu, A., & Andriushchenko, M. (2026). LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces. arXiv:2609.30266.
passages: These analyses assume that LLM agents cannot tamper with their own execution traces.
We advise practitioners to ensure trace logging happens through an independent interception mechanism outside of the agent's control
sources.use: Asks whether the record outlives the agent's own hand. In this house the record is Git, which the machines write themselves; the census found no rewritten process entry, but the record keeps what was done, not who meant it.

sources.cite: Horikawa, K., Li, H., Kashiwa, Y., Ouatiti, Y. E., Sayagh, M., Adams, B., Iida, H., & Hassan, A. E. (2026). Agent or Human? Detecting Commits by AI Coding Agents in the Absence of Authorship Signatures. arXiv:2610.36229.
passages: These signatures are optional, can be removed, and are often attached to pull requests rather than to individual commits.
At the observed Agent share, however, the best detector on the full test set reaches a precision of only 0.332.
signature-free detection can prioritize commits for review but cannot replace recorded attribution
sources.use: Measures, across 1,226 repositories, how far a commit can be told to be an agent's once its signature is gone. This house has no signature on most of its machines' commits by its own rule: 69 of the 80 deeds found carry the architect's name.
